A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Structured Episodic Event Memory (SEEM). Their text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A-C are available and can be matched reliably across additions, renumbering, and pagination changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original LoCoMo and LongMemEval evaluations, component ablations, retrieval sensitivity results, and appendix experiments covering GPT-OSS-120B and incremental memory construction.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds evaluations using Pangu-Embedded-7B on both benchmarks in Table 3.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same dual-layer architecture, event extraction and fusion, graph retrieval, and Reverse Provenance Expansion. Appendix C's prompts are unchanged. Pangu-Embedded-7B is an additional experimental backbone, rather than a revised SEEM procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate LoCoMo and LongMemEval with the same task coverage. The added Pangu experiment changes the model configuration, without introducing a new dataset, domain, population, or task scenario.

E2.justification: New Table 3 introduces a Context (Relevant Only) comparator absent from v1, alongside existing NV-Embed-v2 and HippoRAG 2 comparators. Comparator membership in the retained experiments is unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 4.4 adds a Pangu-Embedded-7B evaluation configuration. Its Table 3 reports EM on both benchmarks and F1 on LongMemEval, extending the previously reported metric set. The existing experiments' stated backbones, retrieval budgets, and evaluation procedures remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The Pangu experiment extends the backbone robustness analysis to a smaller model, testing whether SEEM's benefits persist at 7B parameters. Existing component ablations, retrieval sensitivity, incremental construction, case studies, and Appendix B analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or random-seed protocols, confidence intervals, error bars, or statistical significance tests. The new table follows the existing practice of reporting point scores.

E6.justification: Table 3 adds Pangu results: SEEM scores 48.60 F1, 30.80 EM, and 56.11 J on LoCoMo, and 45.50 F1, 29.60 EM, and 60.80 accuracy on LongMemEval. It exceeds NV-Embed-v2 and HippoRAG 2 there, while Context (Relevant Only) has higher J (69.28) and accuracy (68.60). Retained main-text and appendix results are unchanged.

T1.justification: The problem formulation, event-frame and relational-quadruple definitions, and Equations (1)-(6) are unchanged. No new formal assumptions, mathematical derivations, theorems, or proofs are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same claims about hierarchical episodic memory, provenance-based context reconstruction, and advantages over retrieval baselines. The added experiment supplies further evidence without revising these central statements.

C2.justification: Section 5.1 adds an interpretation that dense, coherent episodic context particularly benefits smaller models, narrows their gap with larger models, and enables parameter-efficient reasoning. Earlier interpretations and the limitations concerning computational cost, error propagation, and predefined semantic slots remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 4.4 now identifies Pangu-Embedded-7B and its parameter count as an additional backbone. Existing retrieval counts, the expansion-budget cap, and Appendix C's implementation prompts are unchanged; no additional hardware, runtime, or resource-access information is supplied.

R1.justification: v2 adds Chen et al. (2025), Pangu Embedded, to document the additional backbone. Section 2 and the positioning against prior retrieval and memory frameworks otherwise remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Section 4.4 receives a localized expansion, and Section 5.1 gains an Efficacy on Parameter-Constrained Backbones paragraph. The overall narrative, section order, and appendix organization are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds Table 3, renumbers the former Tables 3-11 as Tables 4-12, and reflows nearby text and Figure 3. Existing figures and tables retain their content; the presentation changes are localized.

improvement.justification: The added 7B experiment modestly strengthens evidence for portability beyond v1's 80B and 120B backbones. This benefit is qualified by unmeasured efficiency claims and misleading highlighting in Table 3: SEEM is bolded for J and accuracy despite higher Context (Relevant Only) scores. The additional evidence is useful, but supports narrower conclusions than the new discussion suggests.
